dimensions.description: Final outcomes are correct and grounded in observable tool results: transitions are selected from jira.listTransitions by transitionId, jira.transitionIssue succeeds, and jira.getIssue confirms status/resolution; creations/updates succeed with expected end states; no claims of change without matching tool evidence.

Tool calls are planned and ordered correctly: discovery precedes action (e.g., listTransitions before transition), appropriate use of search/get for planning, minimal yet sufficient steps, and avoidance of skipped or redundant steps across heterogeneous workflows.

Parameters are precise and valid: correct identity forms (assigneeAccountId vs display name), valid enums (priority, resolution), correct project/issue keys, use of transitionId rather than status names, and updates limited to intended fields.

The agent faithfully captures user intent, clarifies underspecified requests, maps natural language to exact tool parameters, scopes bulk actions appropriately with filters/limits (e.g., projectKey, status, labels, maxResults), and obtains explicit confirmation before executing destructive or bulk operations.

Strict adherence to synthetic-only and data-provenance requirements: no production identifiers are used or echoed; potential PII or real-looking IDs are redacted; when inputs appear real, the assistant states synthetic/provenance safeguards and refuses to operate on production data.

Errors from tools (e.g., permission_denied, not_found, invalid_transition, validation_error) are surfaced with actionable explanations; the agent retries appropriately or takes alternative paths, requests clarification when needed, and verifies post-remediation state.

The assistant's summaries clearly enumerate actions taken and outcomes with concrete identifiers (issueKey(s), final status/resolution), enabling auditors to verify results from the transcript without ambiguity.
Other important quality factors not covered by listed criteria.
